module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 713

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/713](https://www.erdosproblems.com/713)
- [Er67d] Erdős, P., *Some recent results on extremal problems in graph theory. {R}esults*. (1967),
  117--123 (English); pp. 124--130 (French).
- [ErSi70] Erdős, P. and Simonovits, M., *Some extremal problems in graph theory*. Combinatorial
  theory and its applications, I-III (Proc. Colloq., Balatonfüred, 1969) (1970), 377-390.
- [FrFu87] Frankl, P. and Füredi, Z., *Exact solution of some Turán-type problems*. J. Combin.
  Theory Ser. A (1987), 226--262.
- [FuGe21] Füredi, Zoltán and Gerbner, Dániel, *Hypergraphs without exponents*. J. Combin. Theory
  Ser. A (2021), Paper No. 105517, 9.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter SimpleGraph

namespace Erdos713

open scoped Classical in
/--
Is it true that, for every bipartite graph $G$, there exists some $\alpha\in [1,2)$ and $c>0$ such that $$\mathrm{ex}(n;G)\sim cn^\alpha?$$

The condition that $G$ have at least two edges excludes degenerate forbidden graphs whose
extremal number is eventually zero, for which the displayed asymptotic with $c>0$ is impossible.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_713.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (q : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin q)), G.IsBipartite → 2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card →
      ∃ α c : ℝ, α ∈ Set.Ico 1 2 ∧ 0 < c ∧
        Asymptotics.IsEquivalent atTop
          (fun n : ℕ => (extremalNumber n G : ℝ))
          (fun n : ℕ => c * (n : ℝ) ^ α) := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/--
Must $\alpha$ be rational?

The same nondegeneracy condition on $G$ is used as in part (i). Rationality means that the real
number $\alpha$ lies in the image of the canonical embedding $\mathbb{Q}\to\mathbb{R}$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_713.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (q : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin q)), G.IsBipartite → 2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card →
      ∀ α c : ℝ, α ∈ Set.Ico 1 2 → 0 < c →
        Asymptotics.IsEquivalent atTop
          (fun n : ℕ => (extremalNumber n G : ℝ))
          (fun n : ℕ => c * (n : ℝ) ^ α) →
        α ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℚ → ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos713

reformulations.difference: The source asks about 'every bipartite graph G'. The Lean quantifies only over bipartite G : SimpleGraph (Fin q) that also satisfy `2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: I proved in Lean, for every G on Fin q, that `2 ≤ #G.edgeFinset ↔ ¬ (fun n => (extremalNumber n G : ℝ)) =ᶠ[atTop] 0`. One direction: a graph with at most one edge embeds into any graph on n ≥ q vertices that has an edge, so ex(n;G) = 0 for n ≥ q. The other: with ≥ 2 edges, the single-edge graph on n ≥ 2 vertices is G-free, so ex(n;G) ≥ 1. I also proved that an eventually-zero function is never ~ c·n^α with c > 0. So the Lean right-hand side is provably equivalent to: 'for every bipartite G whose extremal function is not eventually zero, there are α ∈ [1,2) and c > 0 with ex(n;G) ~ c n^α'. This is the source's question with only the degenerate forbidden graphs removed. For those graphs the displayed asymptotic cannot hold. Without the hypothesis the statement is false for a trivial reason: I refuted the unrestricted version with the edgeless graph on Fin 0, for which ex(n;G) = 0 for all n. The docstring states this restriction and its reason correctly. Restricting to graphs on Fin q loses nothing, because extremalNumber is invariant under isomorphism.

reformulations.difference: The Lean adds the hypothesis `2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card`, which the source does not have. The implicit hypotheses α ∈ [1,2) and c > 0 are made explicit.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: I proved in Lean that the right-hand side of part (ii) is equivalent to the same statement quantified over ALL bipartite G, with no edge-count hypothesis. For G with ≤ 1 edge, ex(n;G) is eventually 0, so the hypothesis `ex ~ c n^α` with c > 0 cannot be satisfied and the implication holds vacuously. The hypotheses α ∈ [1,2) and 0 < c are automatic whenever ex(n;G) ~ c n^α for a bipartite G with ≥ 2 edges: ex(n;G) ≥ ⌊n/2⌋ forces α ≥ 1, Kővári–Sós–Turán forces α < 2, and c ≤ 0 is impossible. So they do not restrict the claim. (This last point is argued by hand, not in Lean.)

reformulations.difference: 'Must α be rational?' is formalised as a conditional: for every bipartite G and every α, c with ex(n;G) ~ c n^α, α is rational. It is not formalised as 'for every G there is a rational α with ex(n;G) ~ c n^α', the combined form in which the Füredi–Simonovits survey states the Erdős–Simonovits conjecture.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: When the exponent exists for G, it is unique: c n^α ~ c' n^β forces α = β. So 'must α be rational' literally means 'every exponent that occurs is rational', which is exactly the Lean conditional. The combined existential form is equivalent to parts (i) ∧ (ii) together, so the file loses nothing. The two readings differ only if part (i) fails. In that case the conditional reading keeps question 2 meaningful, which fits the source's separate phrasing. This is a reading of the wording, not a formal equivalence, so it is not proved in Lean.

review.notes:
The source is erdosproblems.com/713; the LaTeX source was read verbatim. It says: "Is it true that, for every bipartite graph G, there exists some α∈[1,2) and c>0 such that ex(n;G)∼cn^α? Must α be rational?" Both declarations follow it: `extremalNumber` is ex(n;·), `IsEquivalent atTop` is ∼ against c·n^α with Real.rpow, `Set.Ico 1 2` is [1,2), and rationality is `Set.range Rat.cast`. `answer(sorry)` comes before all quantifiers, as the conventions require.

Status: the source records the problem as OPEN, and the teorth database agrees. Both theorems are tagged `research open`, so there is no status issue. The module docstring's references match the site's reference list exactly.

Lean checks (in /workspace/review; all compile without `sorry`):
1. scratch1.lean refutes part (i) without the edge-count hypothesis, using the edgeless graph on Fin 0. So the hypothesis is needed.
2. scratch3.lean proves:
   - ex(n;G) = 0 for n ≥ q when G has ≤ 1 edge;
   - ex(n;G) ≥ 1 for n ≥ 2 when G has ≥ 2 edges;
   - so `2 ≤ #edges` is equivalent to 'ex(·;G) not eventually zero';
   - the stated equivalences for both parts.

Neither part is trivially provable or refutable. For P_3, ex(n;P_3) = ⌊n/2⌋ ~ n/2, so the hypothesis of part (ii) can be satisfied, and the stated asymptotic is exactly the open question.

The source's weaker variant, ex(n;G) ≍ n^α, is not formalised. That is an optional addition, not a defect.

The original Erdős papers on the Rényi archive are image-only scans and I could not read them. For the wording I relied on erdosproblems.com and the Füredi–Simonovits survey.
